subject: Renewal: commit flex escape hatch and short-term price hold
messages:
From: Marco Silva <marco.silva@cobaltcommerce.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@cobaltcommerce.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — price hold + capacity uplift

Hi Priyom,

Hope you had a good week. Our current term with Redwood is up at the end of January and usage is trending up faster than forecasted — we expect a sustained ~40% uplift in embedding + chat traffic in Q1 (new features rolling out). Before we get into procurement redlines, two asks from my side to accelerate discussion: 

- Can Redwood lock current unit pricing for a 12-month window if we commit to a 25% capacity increase (committed tokens)?
- Would you consider an upfront operational credit to offset migration and burst costs while we ramp (we were thinking ~$100k)?

We prefer a short, simple renewal with a single SOW amendment rather than a lengthy amendment. If you have an options matrix (short price-hold + true-up path / multi-year discount / credits), send it over and we can prioritize.

Thanks — aim to finalize before our budget review 1/12.

Marco Silva
VP Procurement, Cobalt Commerce
marco.silva@cobaltcommerce.com
+1 415-555-0194

Attachment: Cobalt_Renewal_Request_2026.pdf (customer renewal ask summary)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco.silva@cobaltcommerce.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@cobaltcommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — price hold + capacity uplift

Marco — really appreciate the clarity and the timeline. High level options we can put on the table quickly: 

1) 12-month price hold + tiered commit increase (25% uplift): 10% renewal discount applied to list for first year; a one-time operational credit ($100k) that offsets onboarding/burst; true-up at quarter end with a 90-day escape hatch for under-commit protection.

2) 24-month term with a graduated discount (6% Y1 / 3% Y2), smaller credit ($40k), and committed baseline increase (15%).

3) Short-term hold (6 months) + temporary burst pool providing extra capacity at a reduced overage rate. No long-term commitment change.

I attached a draft term-sheet (initial-term-sheet-v1.docx) with Option 1 spelled out — it maps to your request. I want to loop in legal/finance for a quick estimate on P&L impact; cc'ing internal leads to expedite. Would you prefer we do Option 1 with the escape hatch clarified, or do you want to see the 24-month alternative?

Next steps: if Option 1 looks reasonable I can move to an internal approval request today and follow up with a concrete DocuSign proposal.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: initial-term-sheet-v1.docx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Renewal discussion — price hold + capacity uplift (need quick approval)

Ben / Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Marco's ask and my proposed Option 1. TL;DR: customer asks for 12-month price hold if they increase committed capacity by ~25% plus a $100k operational credit. I proposed: 10% renewal discount on list for 12 months, $100k credit, 90-day escape hatch on the uplift to protect Redwood for under-commit, quarter-end true-up.

Why I like this: keeps renewal simple, secures committed uplift which helps capacity planning and gives us visibility on demand. Concerns: $100k credit + 10% discount hits gross margin — need to confirm acceptable. I ran a quick back-of-envelope: blended unit margin impact is ~6.1% on ARR for year 1 versus baseline.

Suggested internal concession variant (if we need to tone this down): 7% discount + $75k one-time credit; price hold shortened to 9 months (still gives customer pricing predictability but reduces downside).

Questions for internal reviewers: 
- Finance: is the proposed blended impact (6.1%) within the tolerance band for renewals at this ACV?
- Sales Ops / CS: can we operationalize the 90-day escape hatch (mechanics on true-up, notifications, and usage measurement)?
- Legal: any red flags on the scope of price-hold language vs. export/region clauses?

Please reply with Approve / Approve with edits / Reject. Marco needs a committed path by EOD Wednesday 12/16 to hit his procurement window.

Quoted message below.

Marissa / Jordan — if you both confirm operationally we can accept that and I'll route to finance for sign-off. If Legal wants to tweak language, we should aim for redlines within 24 hours to meet Marco's procurement cutoff.

Marco / Priya — thank you for the quick turnaround. We discussed internally and can proceed on a middle-path that preserves predictability while limiting financial exposure: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-02-01)
- Commit uplift: +20% baseline committed tokens (customer to confirm exact baseline by 12/20)
- Pricing: 7% one-time renewal discount applied to list for first 9 months (9-month price hold)
- Credit: $75,000 one-time operational credit applied to first invoice after amendment signature
- Escape hatch / true-up: 90-day window after effective date; usage below uplifted commit triggers a pro-rated true-up invoice (no penalty), measured at the agreed unit rates; customer can de-escalate commit once during the 90-day window with written notice
- Attachments: updated term sheet (attached) and DocuSign link will follow for signature.

Next steps: I'll send an updated DocuSign with the redlined SOW and the credit applied. Priya, can you confirm the baseline committed tokens by end of day Monday (12/20)? Once we have that we can finalize the amendment and circulate a signed copy.

If that looks good I will circulate DocuSign now and expect countersignature within 48 hours for your procurement deadline.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
